topic: Demonstration and explanation on aircraft marshalling procedure during taxing / aircraft movement.
syllabus_extract: Demonstration and explanation on aircraft marshalling procedure during taxing / aircraft movement.
specific_objectives: 29.1.1.7 Trainee will be able to explain the aircraft marshalling procedure.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of marshaller positioning, hand signals for start/stop/turn, and safety precautions during aircraft movement under instructor supervision.
intro_questions: What is the primary role of a marshaller during aircraft movement?
List three safety precautions required before an aircraft begins taxiing.
Where should the marshaller stand relative to the aircraft nose?

development.content:
Marshaller positioning and visibility
Standard hand signals for movement
Communication with pilot via radio
Emergency stop procedures
Safety zones and exclusion areas

topics: Use of light bars and reflectors
development.content:
Taxi route adherence and markings
Handling specific aircraft types
Coordination with ground crew
Night marshalling procedures
Use of light bars and reflectors

Practical demonstration of signals
Safety checks before movement
Instructor supervision protocols
Correct marshaller stance
Signal clarity and visibility checks

summary_questions: Explain the difference between the 'Stop' and 'Hold' signals in marshalling.
Describe the correct positioning of the marshaller when guiding an aircraft turn.
What actions must be taken if the marshaller loses visual contact with the pilot?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report on the specific marshalling signals required for the aircraft type discussed in LP 02, focusing on start and stop procedures.

pft_rows.syllabus: Demonstration and explanation on the correct procedures of connecting the towing arm to A/C and tractor and movement of aircraft with proper positioning of safety numbers and choke man i.a.w INAP 2 article
